jobs.description:
**About Anthropic**
-------------------

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

**About the role**
------------------

Reinforcement learning is how Claude learns to reason, write code, and act autonomously over long horizons. At frontier scale, an RL run is a large distributed system: training, sampling, and environment execution run concurrently across a large fleet of accelerators and hosts. As an engineer in RL Engineering, you'll work on keeping that system secure as it scales.

This is a hands-on engineering role. You'll work in the RL codebase and the infrastructure underneath it, alongside the engineers and researchers who build and use it. The system is large and changes as fast as the research does, so security work here has to keep up with that pace without costing performance or velocity.

We're hiring from two backgrounds: security engineers who want to work on large-scale ML systems, and ML systems or research engineers who want to work on security. Strong candidates have depth in one and real interest in the other.

**Key responsibilities**
------------------------

* Design, build, and operate security controls for RL training systems and the infrastructure they run on
* Work across the stack (orchestration, environments, training, inference) wherever the work is needed
* Review designs and code across the RL stack, find security problems, and fix them
* Build shared libraries and tooling that other RL engineers and researchers build on
* Build the observability needed to understand what these systems are doing
* Work with researchers and performance engineers to make sure security changes preserve training correctness and performance
* Write clear design documents for what you build

* Strong software engineering skills in Python and at least one systems language such as Rust, C++, or Go
* Experience designing, building, and operating large-scale distributed systems or security systems in production
* Strong understanding of security fundamentals
* Working knowledge of Linux, containers, and cloud infrastructure
* Experience debugging complex problems across many hosts and services
* Ability to reason about tradeoffs between security, performance, and reliability
* Strong written communication, including design documents

* Experience running ML training or inference infrastructure at scale

* Experience with container orchestration such as Kubernetes, and with sandboxed or virtualized code execution at scale
* Experience building observability for large fleets
* Experience supporting research teams or other fast-moving internal users
* Familiarity with reinforcement learning or large language model training workloads

**About Plato**
===============

Plato is an applied research lab building the foundational infrastructure to train specialized AI agents.

We turn real-world data streams into high-fidelity simulated environments that generate the training signal needed to make capable models. Our work supports frontier labs, hyperscalers, and enterprises building AI systems for complex, high-stakes work.

Today, only a handful of players can train models for capable work. Compute and algorithms are rapidly commoditizing, but reinforcement learning data remains the bottleneck. Plato is changing that by automatically scaling training environments from proprietary real-world data.

**Why Apply**
=============

* Work with the frontier: Build safety environments and benchmarks that research teams at leading AI labs can use to measure emerging capabilities and misaligned behavior.
* Real ownership: Help set Plato’s safety evaluation agenda, from the research questions worth testing to the evidence we share with lab partners.
* Research to production: Work with engineers to turn experimental designs into runnable environments, with a short path from an idea to an evaluation labs can use.

**The Role**
============

Plato is hiring an individual contributor researcher to design safety environments and benchmarks, starting with evaluations that measure how well AI models can improve themselves and other models.

You will establish a new research direction at Plato, designing safety-relevant benchmarks and working with engineers to turn them into runnable environments. Your initial focus will be measuring AI R&D capabilities, including experiment design, model training, and research replication.

You will also investigate reward hacking, sabotage, deception, and other misaligned behavior. The work spans research design, empirical evaluation, and failure analysis, with substantial ownership of the research agenda. Some environments may also be used in training to reduce the behaviors they reveal.

**What You’ll Do**
==================

* Design Safety Benchmarks: Measure AI research automation and self-improvement. Define tasks, baselines, budgets, and success criteria that separate meaningful progress from superficial completion.
* Build Safety Environments: Design environments that expose reward hacking, sabotage, deception, and failures to follow intended constraints.
* Hold the Evaluation Bar: Investigate contamination, grader weaknesses, task ambiguity, and shortcuts that could make a result misleading.
* Track Frontier Capabilities: Run experiments with current models, inspect trajectories and failures, and measure how capabilities change across models and over time.
* Work with Engineering: Turn research designs into reproducible environments with clear scoring, useful instrumentation, and documented limitations.
* Share the Findings: Translate results into benchmark releases, research reports, and concrete recommendations for lab partners.

**Required Qualifications**
===========================

* Recent Research: Hands-on work in frontier-model evaluation, benchmarks, or AI safety in the past one to two years.
* Research Track Record: Meaningful contributions to papers, released benchmarks, public reports, or comparable empirical work. We care about the quality of your work and your contribution more than credentials or years of experience.

* Experimental Judgment: You can explain what an evaluation measures, how it could be gamed, and which conclusions its results do and do not support.
* Research Ownership: Ability to turn an ambiguous question into a concrete experimental design and collaborate closely with engineers to implement it.

* A software engineering background or programming skills that let you implement environments, evaluation harnesses, and analysis tools yourself.
